chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hajjaj from Ali ibn Uqba from Muhammad ibn Muslim, and he was the brother-in-law of Burayd al-Ijli, who said:

Burayd said to Muhammad: Ask Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about something I intend to do. Indeed, people have deposits and wealth in my hand which I circulate in. So I wish to withdraw from the world and give each person with a right their right. He said: So Muhammad asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about that and informed him of the story, and said: What do you think regarding him? He said: 'O Muhammad, does he start by fighting (with his debtors)? No, but he takes and gives upon Allah (the Mighty and Majestic).'
ai.seo_question: How should a merchant settle debts and deposits when retiring from business according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Burayd al-Ijli seeks guidance from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding the ethical management of debts and deposits (*wadai'*) while transitioning from commerce. The Imam advises against aggressive litigation or immediate full repayment, which might be financially ruinous, but rather recommends a gradual, proportional settlement (*yakhudh wa yu'ti*) while maintaining reliance on Allah (*'ala Allah*). This reflects the Shia juristic principle of balancing financial obligation with practical capability, emphasizing trustworthiness and divine facilitation over rigid, potentially harmful immediacy.
